skill.name: lipsync
skill.description: Creates lip-synced videos through the RunComfy CLI. It routes existing videos, portraits, or script-only requests to supported lip-sync models.
skill.summary: Route lip-sync requests to RunComfy models for videos, portraits, and script-driven clips.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick and URL findings are Markdown documentation, code fences, placeholders, or catalog links rather than hidden code. Real risks remain because the skill intentionally runs the runcomfy CLI, sends face and voice media to RunComfy services, and relies on operator consent checks for dual-use synthetic media.

remediation.issue: Potential shell quoting failure for --input JSON
remediation.suggestion: Build JSON with a structured encoder and pass it through a file or safely quoted argument. Never concatenate raw user URLs, scripts, or prompts into Bash.
Warn users before sending face, voice, or asset URLs to RunComfy. Document provider, retention, and privacy expectations.
Require explicit confirmation that the face and voice are authorized. Refuse public figures, private people without consent, sexual content, and defamatory scenarios.
Prefer pinned versions or existing trusted installs. Avoid npx -y in automated flows unless the package and version are reviewed.

content.value_statement: Lip-sync workflows often require choosing between many video and avatar models. This skill routes each request to the right RunComfy model and command pattern.
actual_capabilities: Routes source video plus audio requests to Sync Labs or Kling lip-sync models.
Routes portrait plus audio requests to OmniHuman talking-head generation.
Creates runcomfy run command patterns with model names, inputs, and output folders.
Explains when to use premium, batch, avatar, or script-only lip-sync routes.
Lists relevant RunComfy catalog pages, exit codes, and troubleshooting references.
Includes consent, token storage, endpoint allowlist, and generated-file size guidance.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy token before generation can run.
Sends media URLs or assets to RunComfy and model providers for processing.
Does not verify consent or prevent impersonation on its own.
Output quality depends on audio clarity, face framing, model limits, and duration match.

use_cases.title: Localize a brand video
use_cases.description: Sync a translated voiceover to an existing approved video while preserving the original scene.

use_cases.title: Create a talking-head ad
use_cases.description: Turn a consented portrait and voiceover into a short presenter clip for campaigns.

use_cases.title: Compare lip-sync routes
use_cases.description: Choose between Sync Labs, OmniHuman, Kling, and Creatify based on input type and quality needs.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner video sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lipsync skill to sync my approved source video with my approved voiceover. Prefer the highest quality route and explain the selected model.

prompt_templates.title: Portrait avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking-head video from this consented portrait and voiceover. Choose the RunComfy route for avatar-style generation.

prompt_templates.title: Model selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my lip-sync goal, inputs, budget, and quality needs. Recommend the best RunComfy model before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Multilingual campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multilingual lip-sync workflow for one approved identity and several approved audio tracks. Include model choices, review steps, and consent checks.

output_examples.input: An approved product video and a Spanish voiceover for the same speaker.
output: Selected Sync Labs sync v2 Pro for high mouth fidelity on existing footage.
Prepared the RunComfy route with source video, voiceover, and local output folder.
Recommended reviewing timing, identity match, and disclosure before publication.

output_examples.input: A consented creator portrait and a short product pitch audio file.
output: Selected OmniHuman because the input is a portrait plus audio.
Prepared an avatar-style generation route for a talking-head clip.
Flagged audio clarity, portrait framing, and consent as required checks.

output_examples.input: A script for a social clip, with no recorded voiceover available.
output: Recommended a script-driven route such as Kling text-to-video or HappyHorse.
Explained that generated audio may not match a specific speaker voice.
Suggested recording approved audio first if exact voice matching is required.

best_practices: Use only consented face, voice, and video assets for every lip-sync job.
Use clean isolated speech and match audio length to the source video.
Review token storage, external processing, and output folders before running commands.
anti_patterns: Do not target public figures or private people without explicit consent.
Do not paste secrets into prompts, filenames, audio metadata, or asset URLs.
Do not run unverified installer scripts or unreviewed command strings.

faq.question: Does this skill generate lip-synced video directly?
faq.answer: It prepares and runs RunComfy CLI workflows. Generation happens through RunComfy models and requires an authenticated account.

faq.question: Which inputs are supported?
faq.answer: It supports existing video plus audio, portrait plus audio, and script-only requests for supported routes.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill environments.

faq.question: Does it verify consent automatically?
faq.answer: No. Users and operators must verify rights for the face, voice, source video, and final use.

faq.question: Where does media processing happen?
faq.answer: The workflow sends inputs to RunComfy model endpoints and downloads generated outputs to the selected local folder.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing output?
faq.answer: Review identity authorization, voice authorization, timing quality, disclosure needs, and platform policy requirements.
